118592.name: Chabad of Topanga
118592.note: Topanga Messenger, June 19 2003 ('Torah, Torah, Torah – Chabad Comes to Topanga', by Susan Chasen; California Digital Newspaper Collection): Rabbi Dovid Weiss called residents as 'Rabbi Weiss from Chabad of Topanga' — 'That's because it's brand new'; 'Dovid and his wife Nechama Dina have just moved to Topanga with their two daughters ... to establish a Chabad center here'; the canyon was unfamiliar to them 'until about two months ago'; it was one of Chabad's '20 new West Coast centers' that year, and for five years before he had been a rabbi at Chabad of Brentwood. Dec 18 2003: 'Rabbi Dovid Weiss who recently established Chabad of Topanga'. Times of Israel (Jan 2025): 'for over 20 years'.

earlier.where: the Weisses' rented home on Glen Trail (gatherings at their home or others' houses; the Community House rented for holidays)

117579.name: Chabad of Westlake Village
117579.note: Thousand Oaks Star, Aug-Nov 1985 (California Digital Newspaper Collection): Rabbi Yitzchok Sapochkinsky first appears in Aug 1985 as 'the newly appointed educational director of Chabad of the [Conejo]', and on Sept 6 1985 Chabad's 'afternoon Hebrew School with newly appointed Rabbi Yitzchok Sapochkinsky as principal will open Wednesday at Suite E 741 [Lakefield Road]' in Westlake Village; his name is not in the paper before 1985 although it covers Chabad from 1977. The name 'Chabad of Westlake Village' (741 Lakefield Road, Suite D) is in the paper from Nov 1993. Medium: in 1985 it was Chabad of the Conejo's Westlake Village branch, and when it took its own name isn't known. (therebbesimpact.com: 1985.) Now at 2524 Townsgate Rd (chabad.org; 530 Hampshire Rd in a 2024 brochure).

earlier.where: 741 Lakefield Road, Suites D and E, Westlake Village (from 1985: the Hebrew School; 'Chabad of Westlake Village' there in 1993-1999)
